Data Collection: Tools that help structure and organise exposure data gathering. Typically used at the very start of an assessment, before any modelling.
Basic Characterization: Simple instruments for initial hazard and exposure characterisation, useful for screening and prioritisation.
Preliminary / Initial Exposure Assessmen: Qualitative or semi-quantitative tools that produce a first estimate of exposure, often through control banding or a tiered scoring approach.
Refined Exposure Assessment: Quantitative models that produce scenario-specific exposure estimates, sometimes including probabilistic or Bayesian treatment of uncertainty.
Validating Exposure Assessments: Tools used to test or confirm an exposure assessment against measurement data or an alternative method.
Product Exposure Modeling: Models built for consumer product scenarios, accounting for formulation, use pattern, frequency, and consumer behaviour.
Environmental Risk / Exposure Assessment: Tools focused on environmental release, indoor and outdoor fate and transport, and community or ecosystem exposure.
